title: McKinney's Cotton Pickers, Horvath and the WGN band
summary: Charlie Horvath promoted the Cotton Pickers and organized Goldkette's WGN band, which sold poorly next to the Victor records.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: What about McKinney's? That's another band.

McKinney's Cotton Pickers? Well, they originated in Detroit. Uh, they were organized and promoted principally by George Horvath, who's dead now. And, uh, he's, uh, Charlie Horvath, I mean. Charlie Horvath. He was a promoter for the Goldcat Enterprises, as they call them. Goldcat never did promote anything. He could sell. He was a good salesman. He could go there and sell. But, uh, promoting anything, Charlie Horvath was the one, the real promoter. And he'd, uh, he promoted the Cotton Pickers. After the Victor Band broke up, why, he'd promote the Cotton Pickers. And he also organized the WGN Band in Chicago. And, uh, I guess you got a record of that, uh, of that Goldcat outfit, hasn't it? Yeah. Under the direction of Stokes, Harold Stokes? Yeah. Harold Stokes was, uh, uh... That was the other Goldcat, Guillaume. Mm-hmm. But that, uh, they made quite a number of records, but their records didn't sell anything in comparison to the Victor records, so...
You got the, uh, box there you want to put the machine up so you can hear some of them?
You better shut that off, huh? Yeah, cut it off in there.
